Formulation
Predisposing: Long-standing occupation involving chemical cleaners; pre-existing dry skin.  
Precipitating: Recent job change with continued exposure and inconsistent glove use.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing chemical exposure, pain, and functional limitation; potential loss of income/time off work.  
Protective: Insight into occupational trigger; willingness to comply with treatment; minimal alcohol use; no substance use.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Reduce hand pain/itching to resume work comfortably.  
  • Prevent further skin cracking and associated distress.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Alleviate contact dermatitis symptoms within 10–14 days.  
  • Minimize occupational stress by enabling return to duties.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Consistently wear protective gloves during all cleaning tasks.  
  • Apply prescribed topical steroid and emollient 3–4 times daily for two weeks.  
  • Monitor symptoms; return earlier if worsening.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide prescriptions for medium-potency topical steroid and appropriate emollient.  
  • Educate on trigger avoidance and skin care regimen.  
  • Arrange review in 1–2 weeks or sooner if deterioration.

Secondary Problem (Adjustment difficulties):
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Adapt to new work environment with reduced stress.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Screen for emerging anxiety/depressive symptoms at follow-up.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Observe mood/stress levels; note any impact on sleep or daily functioning.  
  • Report psychological distress at review.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Conduct brief mental health screening (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) at next visit.  
  • Consider counseling referral if adjustment issues persist.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Dermatitis pathophysiology, glove use, skin hydration, medication application, when to seek urgent care.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased redness, spread of rash, bleeding, severe pain, inability to work.
- Coping Strategies: Strict trigger avoidance, regular moisturization, prompt medical review if symptoms recur.
